note: Every number carries its source ids and tier; see docs/ANIM3D-NOTES.md

common_time.note: common time (drill-ground cadence for recruits and the manual of arms)

quick_time.note: same step length as common time; 110 a minute

route_step.note: swiftness of the route step 110 a minute "habitually maintained in columns in route"; the step length is not restated (28 in. of the direct step assumed: inferred)

double_quick_urgent.note: "under urgent circumstances" the cadence may be increased to 180; 4,000 yards in about 25 minutes (Hardee)

backward.note: march backwards: 14 in. heel to heel, always in quick time (paras 246-248)

run.note: H.S.S. para 116: the run follows the principles of the double quick, "a greater degree of swiftness"; no rate or step is printed

mark_time.note: the pivot man at a wheel from a halt "only turns in his place" and "will merely mark time"; the cadence of the rank is the quick time 110

wheel_pivot_quick.note: in a wheel in marching the pivot takes steps of nine inches in quick time

wheel_pivot_dq.note: eleven inches in double quick time

wheel_mid25_quick.note: a quarter of the way from the pivot to the wheeling flank: 9 + 0.25 x (28 - 9) inches

wheel_mid75_quick.note: three quarters of the way: 9 + 0.75 x (28 - 9) inches

wheel_flank_quick.note: "will take the full step of twenty-eight inches"

wheel_flank_dq.note: the full step of thirty-three inches in double quick time

motion.exempt: cartridge, rammer and (un)fixing-bayonet motions have no fixed cadence

pause_aim_fire.note: the instructors recommend "a short pause between Aim and Fire" (no length printed): range

muzzle_loader_drill.basis: training standard "at least three rounds in a minute with ease and regularity" taken as the drill pace; 4 rpm = every regulated motion at 1/90 min and the 10 exempt motions at about 0.97 s: the plausible fastest drill cycle

muzzle_loader_battle.basis: weapons.json 2-3 rounds a minute (weak sources: tier inferred); the PDF 2-3 rounds a minute is consistent

repeater_spencer.basis: a Wikipedia rate in weapons.json (weak source), not a combat rate

revolver.basis: no rate in the acquired texts: range chosen so six shots take 15-30 s

field_gun_solid.basis: Gibbon: 30-40 s for a 6-pdr, 60 s for a 12-pdr, mean about one a minute, 2-3 when pressed; Light Artillery Board: 2 solid shot a minute "with sufficient deliberation for pointing"

field_gun_canister.basis: Light Artillery Board planning figure: 3 canisters a minute; Gibbon: 2-3 a minute when pressed

gun_steps.name: Sponge
gun_steps.note: motion count 4 (ART-FA-15); the relative length is the motion count

gun_steps.name: Load
gun_steps.note: No. 2 receives the round from No. 5 and enters it; length authored

gun_steps.name: Point
gun_steps.note: the gunner points (traverse by handspike signal, elevating screw) while No. 3 shifts the trail; length authored

gun_steps.name: Ready
gun_steps.note: No. 3 pricks the cartridge, No. 4 inserts the friction primer and takes the lanyard

gun_steps.name: Run up
gun_steps.note: after the shot the piece is run up to its former place "if necessary" (no recoil distance printed)

gunner.note: at the end of the trail handspike (ART-FA-02)

n1.note: right of the piece, about two feet outside the wheel, abreast the front part of the wheel (guns) (ART-FA-03)

n3.note: right, in line with the knob of the cascable, covering No. 1 (ART-FA-04)

n6.note: behind the limber (at the limber chest) (ART-FA-06); limber pole end 6 yd from the trail handspike end (ART-FA-09)

n8.note: the chief of the caisson, 4 yards behind the limber on its left (ART-FA-07)

chief.note: the chief of the piece opposite the middle of the trail, outside the left cannoneers (ART-FA-08)

recoil.note: rig note: FIGURES models a 0.5-0.6 m run-out (modelled); this table keeps the wider range and the caller picks by the variation scalar

file_fire.note: "each next file aims as the previous file brings its pieces down to reload": the right-hand file begins, each next file aims when its neighbour lowers: the interval is about one motion of Ready/Aim; documented as a rule, the interval is not printed

rank_fire.note: the rear rank fires first, then the front rank; the ranks alternate until "cease firing"

rifle.basis: kit/weapons.json m1861_springfield overall_in 56, barrel_in 40; positions along the stock are inferred, not measured

ramrod.basis: a rifle-musket ramrod is about as long as the barrel less the head; the exact length is not in the acquired texts

gaps.title: Real rate and tempo of fire of a unit at a minute of the battle
gaps.text: Only a training standard (3 rounds a minute), weapons.json rates (2-3, weak sources) and artillery planning rates exist. No unit-level fire tempo, volley synchrony or ammunition expenditure per minute is documented per regiment in the acquired texts.

gaps.title: Officers' actual commands and the men's reaction times
gaps.text: The command vocabulary is documented (Hardee, Casey); which command was given when, and the delay between command and execution, are not.

gaps.title: Misfire rates
gaps.text: The misfire procedure is printed (INF-FIRE-06..08); no rate is in any acquired text. The system emits no misfire unless a scenario sets a rate.

gaps.title: Recoil distance of a field piece
gaps.text: No measured recoil distance in the drill text (ART-FA-14); Gibbon gives only a theoretical free recoil of 17.4 ft for a 12-pdr field gun (derived). A range of 0.9-1.8 m of carriage motion is used.

gaps.title: Lengths of the cartridge and rammer motions
gaps.text: The cartridge, rammer and bayonet motions are exempt from the 1/90-minute cadence (H.S.S. para 130); their lengths are not printed. The loading cycle is fitted to the fire plan's seconds-per-round and the exempt motions share the remainder.

gaps.title: Cadence and step of the run
gaps.text: H.S.S. para 116 says only "a greater degree of swiftness". A range of 190-230 steps a minute and 36-44 in. is used.

gaps.title: Cavalry and horse-artillery gait speeds
gaps.text: Cooke's Cavalry Tactics (1862) and the Light Artillery Board's horse-artillery chapter were not read for gait rates; modern equestrian ranges are used (walk 1.4-1.8, trot 3-4, canter 5-6.5, gallop 7-10 m/s) and marked plausible-procedural.

gaps.title: Cavalry sabre and carbine drill
gaps.text: The cavalry manual was not acquired; sabre cuts, draw/return, mounted and dismounted carbine actions, horse-holding (every fourth man) are authored from the plan's description and general knowledge.

gaps.title: Non-drill activities (digging, chopping, rail piling, stone laying, cooking, sleeping, picket, burial, surgery)
gaps.text: No motion source exists in the acquired texts; the plan allows only "procedural" motion marked as a modern reconstruction. Tool use follows the documented tools where the timeline names them (e.g. spades and shovels at Culp's Hill); the motion is authored.

gaps.title: Wound reactions and fall styles
gaps.text: The history layer decides who falls and when; how a man fell is not documented. Eight fall styles are seeded from the variation scalar.

gaps.title: Stretcher, ambulance and field-hospital handling
gaps.text: The ambulance-corps drill (1864) and stretcher-bearer practice of July 1863 were not acquired; a two-bearer litter carry is authored.

gaps.title: Confederate drill manual and crew practice
gaps.text: Hardee/Casey are US-army texts; which manual each regiment used in June-July 1863 is not stated (DRILL-HARDEE-NOTES section 5). Confederate battery crew size and practice are not in the acquired texts.

gaps.title: Taking cover behind a wall or a tree
gaps.text: The manuals print the kneeling, lying and sitting positions and the bugle calls for skirmishers "lie down" and "rise up" (HAR-S33, HAR-S34, HAR-K05, HAR-L02); how a man used a wall or a tree (crouching behind it, looking round the end, rising to fire over it) is not in any acquired text. The poses are authored from the documented postures.

gaps.title: Steps of the men between the pivot and the wheeling flank
gaps.text: Hardee prints the pivot step (9 / 11 in.) and the flank step (28 / 33 in.) of a wheel (ANIM-H381, ANIM-H382) but not the steps of the men between; they are taken in proportion to the distance from the pivot (geometry of a rank turning about the pivot).

gaps.title: Four-man stretcher, ambulance loading and helping a limping man
gaps.text: The ambulance-corps drill (1864) and the stretcher practice of July 1863 were not acquired. The four-man stretcher (lift, carry, set down), loading a stretcher into an ambulance wagon and supporting a limping man are authored from the description in the plan (render/PLAN.md G9: carrying the wounded: two-man, four-man stretcher, helping a limping man). Extends G-ANIM-11.

gaps.title: Limbering, unlimbering, moving a piece by hand, the prolonge
gaps.text: The ORDER of actions is printed (Instruction for Field Artillery paras 111-112, 115, 126-127, 476-477: ART-FA-70, 71, 73, 74, 90, 93); the body mechanics (lifting the trail on the handspike, keying the pintle, pushing on the spokes, uncoiling the prolonge) and the time each takes are authored.

gaps.title: Horse artillery: mounted cannoneers, drivers, mounting and dismounting
gaps.text: Gibbon: in horse artillery there are 11 cannoneers to each piece, all mounted, with two extra men holding the horses while the others work the piece (ART-GB-30). The riding and the mounting and dismounting motions, and the seat of the driver on the near horse, are authored (the light-artillery chapter on horse artillery and Cooke were not read for motions; see G-ANIM-07).

gaps.title: Paired sabre fights (mounted and dismounted)
gaps.text: The cavalry manual and any fencing manual of the period were not acquired (G-ANIM-08). The exchanges (cut, parry, point, riposte, disengage) are authored as two matched clips whose blades meet at the same contact point at the same instants; they are not a record of any fight.

gaps.title: The skirmisher rush between cover
gaps.text: Documented: a rear-rank man advances 10-12 paces past the front-rank man, halts, fires and reloads (HAR-K04); the calls "double quick", "lie down", "rise up" (HAR-L02). The crouched run between cover, the drop to the prone and the spring up are authored on the run gait (G-ANIM-06).

gaps.title: Gear spring parameters (frequency, damping, mass) of the ten secondary-motion bones
gaps.text: skeleton.json gives each gear bone a spring frequency (3.2-7.5 Hz), damping ratio (0.3-0.55) and relative mass; the values are those of the rig author, not measured on period equipment (render/PLAN.md G7 asks for measurement). The deterministic spring solve is implemented (springs.mjs); no measured data exists to calibrate it.

gaps.title: Terrain test surface is the modern bare-earth DEM
gaps.text: The foot-planting measurements use the own application heightfield (render/prototype/data/height.bin, USGS 3DEP bare earth at about 4 m, modern ground, not the 1863 landscape). The 1863 reconstruction is a separate layer; the planter takes any ground(x, z) function.

gaps.title: Variants per state (render/PLAN.md G9 asks for about six per state)
gaps.text: Round 3: the 38 crowd states (standing, the gaits, the three firing cycles, camp and work loops, lying loops) have six variants each, the clip as authored and five seeded modulations of trunk, head, free arm and carried piece (variants.mjs; the legs of a drilled march are never varied: the step is documented). The ranges are plausible-procedural. Still open: the other G9 states (stretcher, limber, cover, wheel, dress, skirmish, horse artillery, melee, the gun crews) have the 2 to 16 hand-authored variants of the earlier rounds, not six seeded ones.

gaps.title: Steep ground: step-up behaviour, lean, slope classes and speed cap
gaps.text: No acquired text gives a marching or scrambling limit on a slope. Above 28 degrees the foot planter limits the stagger between the feet to 0.30 m (half a stair each side of the hip), leans the body into the hill about the hip (0.5 degree per degree, up to 30), tilts the foot onto the face and places the pelvis so that both legs are inside the knee's reach; classes walk / steep_walk (to 50) / scramble (to 60) / climb, and a speed factor (1 to 28 degrees, 0.5 at 50, 0.15 at 80) for the formation layer. Contact error 4.05 cm at worst up to the DEM's 80.4 degrees. No climbing clip, no hand contacts; the ankle is not clamped on faces steeper than it can take.

gaps.title: The lying load is performed in the prone chest frame
gaps.text: The drill says the lying soldier throws himself on his back to load (INF-LYING-02) and raises the piece vertically to prime (INF-LYING-03). The loading keys of the lying cycle are the standing keys in the chest frame, clamped above the ground plane: the lowest point of hands, piece and ramrod over the cycle is -0.495 m (the ramrod tip during the draw; was -1.01 m). The supine load (roll about the body's long axis, loading keys in the world frame) is open work.

gaps.title: Hand and rifle grip geometry
gaps.text: The drill describes positions as relations (hand embracing the guard, arm nearly straight); the 3D coordinates and the positions of grips along the stock (wrist 0.30 m, guard 0.36 m, lower band 0.85 m) are an authored reading of the M1861 proportions.
